_comment: Cross-language behavioural fixture stream for the incremental-checkpoint
(pattern 1) ES consume engine -- issue #1971.
Consumed identically by:
- analysis/es-consume/tests/test_es_consume.py   (Python engine, canonical)
- ml-worker/es_consume.py's own contract suite   (vendored copy)
- arcane/home/honeypot-attacker-identity-worker/
attacker-identity-worker/esconsume_test.go     (Go reference engine)
Same fixture stream in -> same consumed event sequence and same resulting
checkpoint out, in both languages. Every expectation here was computed by
hand from the documented semantics (docs/ES-CONSUME-PATTERNS.md pattern 1)
and ml-worker/worker.py's #168/#188/#190 behaviour -- NOT generated from
either implementation, which is what makes disagreement between them a
real signal.
Harness protocol shared by both adapters:
- pages model transport responses in order. The FIRST page is served by
the search() call, each subsequent page by scroll_next(); a page whose
"ok" is false makes the adapter raise instead of returning, i.e. it
simulates a mid-scroll transport failure at exactly that point.
- exclude_ids passed to the engine is ALWAYS the initial checkpoint's
seen_ids -- that identity is the poll-loop contract itself (#168), not
a per-case option.
- expected_final_checkpoint = advance_checkpoint(returned_events,
initial_checkpoint) -- the caller-visible next position. When ok is
false this encodes the partial-scroll safety property (#168/#190):
persisting that position is safe because every returned event sorts at
or before everything not yet read.

cases.name: #168 equal-timestamp sibling arriving after the checkpoint was saved is not lost
checkpoint advances to the batch's maximum timestamp keeping only IDs at that timestamp
batch cap keeps the earliest prefix only -- checkpoint never moves past unconsumed events
#188 mid-scroll failure returns the pages already read with ok=false -- and that partial position is safe to checkpoint
#188 requery that contains only already-seen siblings is a successful empty poll, not a failure -- checkpoint unchanged
#168 seen_ids is replaced, not appended: bounded by one timestamp's collision count
